2026-12-26.title: The Praise of the Holy Mother of God
readings: God sent his Son, born of a woman
2026-12-26.alt: On the day after Yaldo the Syriac Churches praise the Mother of God, who gave birth to the Saviour. Season of Yaldo and Denho.
2026-12-26.verse: But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.
theo: The day after Christmas the Syriac tradition turns to the one through whom the Word took flesh. “When the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman.” Mary is not a decoration of the feast but the human door through which God entered history. Because she said yes, “God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, ‘Abba! Father!’” and we are no longer slaves but children and heirs.

The shepherds hurry to Bethlehem and find Mary and Joseph and the child lying in the manger. They tell everyone what the angels said, and all who hear are amazed. “But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.” The crowd is amazed for a moment; Mary keeps and ponders for a lifetime. She is the model of every believer who wants Christmas to last beyond one day.
outline: What do we keep from Christmas when the decorations come down?
Mary, the door of God's coming.
“Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.”
live: Sit before the crib for ten minutes in silence today.
Share with someone one way Christmas touched you.
2026-12-26.prayer: Holy Mother of God, through you the Word took flesh. Teach us to treasure and ponder the mystery of your Son, as the shepherds hurry to see him and the angels sing his glory. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we receive the Body born of the Mother of God, and with her we treasure the mystery in our hearts.

quick: God sent his Son, born of a woman.
The shepherds went with haste to see.
Mary treasured and pondered all these things.
2026-12-26.action: Sit before the crib in silence for ten minutes.
2026-12-26.question: What word of Christmas do I want to keep in my heart?

family.explain: The shepherds told everyone about baby Jesus. Mary kept all these things in her heart and thought about them.
family.intention: We thank God for Mary and for our mothers.
family.ask: Ask: “What did God do for us this Yaldo that we want to remember?”

pm.open: Holy Mary, Mother of God, you treasured all these words in your heart. As we gather, teach us to ponder the mystery of your Son. Amen.
share: Mary treasured and pondered (Luke 2:19). What word or event of Yaldo will I treasure?
Paul says God sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts (Galatians 4:6). Do I pray to God as Abba?
How can I honour Mary in my daily life?
pm.resp: Holy Mother of God, pray for us.
interc: For the Church, that she may treasure the mystery of Christ like Mary.
For mothers, that Mary may protect and guide them.
For those who cannot find silence, that they may learn to ponder.
For expectant mothers and newborn children.
For our families, that we may honour Mary.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son was born of the Virgin Mary, Mother of God. Through her prayers, teach us to treasure your word and to live as your children. Amen.

illus: A mother in Pandalam keeps a small notebook. Every evening of the Yaldo season she writes one thing God did that day. She calls it “my Mary notebook”, because, she says, “Mary treasured things in her heart, and I have a bad memory.”

homily: Dear friends, the day after Yaldo our Church celebrates the Praise of the Holy Mother of God, honouring Mary who gave birth to the Saviour. The Eastern Churches have always joined the Mother to the feast of her Son.

St Paul writes: when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, so that we might receive adoption as children. And because you are children, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, Abba! Father! (Galatians 4:4–6).

Born of a woman. Mary is the bridge by which God entered our humanity. That is why the Church calls her Theotokos, Mother of God: not because she is the source of the divine nature, but because the One born of her is truly God (Council of Ephesus, AD 431).

In the Gospel the shepherds go with haste to Bethlehem and find Mary and Joseph, and the child lying in the manger. They tell what they have heard about the child, and all who hear are amazed. But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart (Luke 2:16–19).
Everyone else is talking and wondering. Mary is silent, treasuring, pondering. She keeps the mystery in her heart and lets it grow. This is how she becomes the first disciple.

After the noise of Yaldo, let us learn from Mary to ponder. Let us take a quiet moment each day this week to sit before the crib and treasure what God has done. And let us praise Mary, as our hymns do, as the one who carried the One whom the heavens cannot contain. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary kept everything about Jesus in her heart. Think about baby Jesus quietly for a minute today!

intro: Praise of the Mother of God.

sub: Isaiah: the young woman shall bear a son, Immanuel.
Through her Son we cry “Abba! Father!”
q: Look, the young woman is with child and shall bear a son, and shall name him Immanuel.
And because you are children, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, “Abba! Father!”
points.apply: Pray the Hail Mary slowly with your family.

sub: Micah: from Bethlehem shall come a ruler.
q: But you, O Bethlehem of Ephrathah, who are one of the little clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for me one who is to rule in Israel,
So they went with haste and found Mary and Joseph, and the child lying in the manger.
points.apply: Visit the crib in your parish church.

sub: The psalmist treasures God's word in his heart.
q: I treasure your word in my heart, so that I may not sin against you.
But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.
points.apply: Sit before the crib in silence for ten minutes.

concl: With her, let us keep and ponder.
